finding.claim: Attacker-supplied callbackUrl from POST /subscribe is stored without validation and later used as the target of an outbound HTTP POST by the recurring notifyAll job. This is blind SSRF to any http/https host the server can reach, including RFC-1918, loopback, and link-local addresses.
finding.source: src/Jobs.java:13 subscribe(String name, String callbackUrl), where callbackUrl comes from the request body (documented at line 12)
finding.sink: src/Jobs.java:21 URI.create(cb) passed to HttpRequest.newBuilder().uri(...), dispatched by client.send at line 24

trace.note: Comment documents POST /subscribe body fields name and callbackUrl. No route or auth code in the repo confirms ingress.
subscribe() takes callbackUrl as a String parameter
callbackUrl is stored verbatim in the static subscriptions map with no parsing, scheme, or host check
notifyAll() iterates subscriptions.values() on a per-minute schedule (comment at line 17)
URI.create(cb) turns the stored string into a URI with no allowlist and no hostname comparison
client.send POSTs the payload. The response is read with BodyHandlers.ofString() but never returned or surfaced to the subscriber, so the SSRF is blind

finding.guards_checked: (1) subscribe() lines 13-15 has no validation: no scheme check, no hostname allowlist, no IP/CIDR block. (2) URI.create only rejects syntactically invalid input; it is not a security control. HttpClient restricts schemes to http/https but not hosts. (3) Redirects: HttpClient.newHttpClient() (line 10) uses the default Redirect.NEVER policy, so there is no redirect-based bypass. (4) Ingress auth for /subscribe cannot be verified from this repo. Rated MEDIUM because the response is not returned (blind), not because of auth. (5) Secondary, not SSRF: client.send has no timeout, so one slow internal target can stall the whole notifyAll loop.

verdict.guard_found: none. subscribe() (src/Jobs.java:13-15) stores callbackUrl verbatim with no scheme, host, or IP check. notifyAll() (lines 18-25) passes it straight to URI.create(cb) at line 21 and client.send at line 24. The only validation in the file is the regex on thumb() (line 30), which is a different function and does not touch subscriptions. The default HttpClient redirect policy is NEVER (line 10), so no redirect bypass. Nothing else in the repo validates the value.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: the body value enters subscribe() at src/Jobs.java:13, is stored unvalidated at line 14, and reaches the outbound POST at lines 21-24 via notifyAll(). The only ingress evidence is the comment at line 12 documenting POST /subscribe with a callbackUrl body field, with no route or auth code in the repo, so the caveat is that exposure and auth are unverified, but nothing indicates the value is admin-only, and the code gives no guard on the path.
